summary: KV cache eviction + autoscale window mismatch causing sustained p99 timeouts on Dedicated reservation
description:
Issue summary: ClearBank reported recurring elevated p99 latency and intermittent 504 timeouts for requests routed to their Dedicated reservation during late-afternoon bursts. Impact: customer-facing latency regressions caused degraded downstream SLAs for their production chat assistants (several requests timed out and were retried). Environment: Dedicated GPU reservation in us-east, mixed short (<=64 tokens) and long (>=1024 tokens) request mix, autoscale policy with 5m smoothing window and min_replicas=2.

Observed behavior: Around 17:30-18:15 UTC on 2026-03-10 we saw sustained p99 increase from ~450ms to >2.5s and request 504s. Grafana shows repeated KV cache evictions coincident with long-sequence traffic spikes; autoscaler did not add capacity quickly due to the configured smoothing window and metric delay. A background maintenance batch (nightly model quantization job) was co-scheduled on a subset of nodes in the reservation causing GPU memory pressure and increased pagefaults. The combination produced head-of-line queueing and GPU serialization leading to timeouts.

Expected behavior: Dedicated reservation should maintain p99 within agreed SLA bounds during expected burst patterns by: (1) KV cache retention for mixed-sequence workloads, (2) autoscaler responding within acceptable window to sustained utilization increases, and (3) isolation preventing co-located batch maintenance from starving inference workloads.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a Dedicated reservation with mixed short and long sequence traffic (simulate 70% short <=64 tokens, 30% long >=1024 tokens) at 80-120% of usual burst throughput for 20+ minutes.
2) Ensure autoscale policy has smoothing/window set to 5 minutes and min_replicas=2.
3) Launch a co-located background batch job that performs model conversion/quantization to force GPU memory pressure on a subset of pods.
4) Observe latency (p95/p99) and request errors in Grafana and query KV cache eviction rate in the metrics dashboard.
5) Observe autoscaler decisions in the controller logs and scaling timelines in the Console activity feed.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 18:00 UTC: Initial alert from ClearBank via Support portal. They attached request IDs and trace IDs.
SRE triage: correlated high KV cache eviction spikes (kv_cache_evictions_total) with long-sequence traffic increase and elevated GPU mem_alloc/free churn.
Heap/profile: GPU pagefault counts increased 4x on nodes where batch job ran; those nodes showed elevated vram_pressure and context-switch counts.

Autoscaler logs: scaling_decision events show threshold crossed at 17:36 but next scale-up executed at 17:43 due to 5m smoothing and metric aggregation window — insufficient for observed drop duration.

Hypothesis: Mixed-sequence requests cause more frequent KV cache churn; with smaller min_replicas and long autoscale smoothing, transient but sustained bursts cause queueing. Co-located batch jobs exacerbated GPU memory pressure resulting in serialization and evictions.
Checked related dashboards: grafana/redwood/dedicated/us-east/reservation-42, kibana/logs/serving-runtime, and console/rollouts for any recent model pin changes (none in past 48h).
Cross-ref Slack: #support (thread sup-904821) has customer traces and initial SRE notes; SRE created incident channel #inc-904821 for coordination.
Linked to historical ticket SUP-31845 for a past autoscale undershoot case; patterns similar but root cause here includes KV thrashing + noisy batch job.
comments: 2026-03-10 18:10 Sophie Lin (Support): Logged initial report and requested request IDs and recent traces. Notified SRE and assigned to Ravi.
2026-03-10 18:25 Ravi Patel (SRE): Confirmed p99 spike in Grafana; starting capture on affected nodes and pinning suspicious batch job. Created incident channel and invited ClearBank SE.
2026-03-10 19:00 ClearBank-SE (customer): Provided additional traces and confirmed issue coincides with their late-afternoon job times.
2026-03-10 19:15 Marco Diaz (Platform Eng): Observed autoscaler smoothing prevented fast ramp; proposed lowering smoothing window and increasing min_replicas as hotfix.

2026-03-11 02:00 Ravi Patel (SRE): Applied hotfix — temporarily set autoscale smoothing to 60s for reservation-42 and raised min_replicas to 4. Immediate improvement in p99 observed (from >2.5s to ~480ms).
2026-03-11 06:30 Sophie Lin (Support): Informed ClearBank of hotfix and requested validation; customer confirmed reduction in timeouts and will monitor next business day.
2026-03-12 09:00 Platform Eng: Scheduled follow-up work to prevent future co-scheduling of heavy batch jobs on Dedicated inference pools and to add KV-cache-aware autoscale signals.
resolution:
Workaround applied (2026-03-11): reduced autoscale smoothing to 60s and increased min_replicas to 4 for the affected Dedicated reservation, and temporarily disabled co-located batch jobs. Result: p99 back within SLA and 504s dropped to zero for the monitoring window.

Permanent fixes planned: 1) Add KV-cache-eviction metric as an autoscaler signal and adjust autoscale policy default for dedicated reservations handling mixed-sequence workloads; 2) enforce scheduler constraints to prevent noisy batch jobs from co-locating with inference pods on Dedicated reservations; 3) add a guardrail to recommend pinning model variants for high long-sequence traffic customers; 4) Confluence runbook updates and a post-incident review scheduled.

Follow-ups: #1 (platform) PR to add kv-cache signal: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345; #2 (ops) Confluence doc update: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Dedicated+Autoscale+Runbook.
